content.comment_body: I have a group of [product_name] devices currently set to the 192.168.0.x network range. For technical reasons, I need to change the network to 192.168.1.x. If I manually update the IP addresses of these [product_name] devices to 192.168.1.x, will they still be able to communicate with each other, or do I need to reconfigure all the links?

If you only update the IP addresses on the [product_name] devices and not in the configuration settings, they will no longer be able to exchange data. You also need to adjust the IP addresses in the connection settings.
Thank you. So, I need to go into each device-to-device connection and change the IP address? Just changing the IPs on the devices and in their programs isn't enough?

You didn't specify the details. I can't tell how many [product_name] devices are communicating. However, if they do interact, you have to update the connection settings for all of these devices within the program.
Thanks, I found an alternative solution at the network level.

analysis.insight_summary: Users explored the impact of updating the IP address range for a set of [product_name] devices on a local network. The main takeaway is that network configuration is closely linked to program settings, so simply changing device IPs doesn't automatically ensure continued communication among devices. Users were uncertain about the full scope of adjustments needed and sought clarification on the required actions for consistent connectivity.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes that by updating device IP addresses and modifying their configurations, device-to-device communication will continue without issues. They would prefer a straightforward way to change the IP range without needing to go through extensive manual reconfiguration.
